subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs & concurrency (recap + next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Grant <ethan.grant@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs & concurrency (recap + next steps)

Hi Ethan / Diane,

Thanks for the time today — good discussion. Quick recap + our proposed next steps so the SRE and infra teams can align: 

Call recap (high level)
- Acme Analytics is evaluating embedding+generation features for the customer-facing search flow.
- Primary perf goals: P95 generation latency <= 250ms for ~512-token responses, consistent streaming start within ~100ms.
- Traffic shape: steady daytime traffic with two short peaks (morning US east, late EU), expected warm concurrency peak ~2.5k parallel requests, sustained concurrent connections ~1k.
- Burst tolerance: up to ~3k for <10 minutes during product launches.

Action items / next steps
1) You to confirm exact concurrency/connection pooling numbers for both steady-state and peak (we discussed in the call).
2) I’ll loop in Marcus (SE) to propose a load-test plan and run a concurrency qualification session.
3) We’ll share Redwood’s default rate limits and a proposal for reserved concurrency / Dedicated capacity if needed.
4) Exchange the SLO table + test plan — attaching a short template for your convenience.

Attachments: concurrency_requirements.xlsx (template)

Questions I have for you now (short):
- For the 2.5k peak, is that concurrent request count at Stripe-style single-tenant per-customer level or aggregate across multiple user sessions?
- Do you need per-connection streaming (server push) or are you fine with chunked responses over HTTP streams?

If it helps, can you send the SRE notes or an internal doc with the expected request distribution? Marcus will use that for the qualification plan.

I’ve penciled in time for a 30–45m load-test prep session next week. Let me know your availability.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134

From: Ethan Grant <ethan.grant@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Diane Lopez <diane.lopez@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T17:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & concurrency (recap + next steps)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear notes. Quick answers and a few details from our side:

- Concurrency breakdown: the 2.5k is aggregate concurrent requests for the public-facing search endpoints across all customers during peak. Typical sustained concurrent requests are ~1k.
- Connection pooling: our frontend uses long-lived HTTP/2 connections from a fleet of edge nodes; we expect ~500 persistent connections with multiplexing.
- Streaming: required. We need the first bytes to start streaming within ~100ms for perceived latency constraints; full 512-token generation can take longer but must remain under the P95 250ms target overall for most queries.
- Retry behavior: we do ~2 retries per failed token-request, backoff jittered.

Attaching our SRE notes (acme-sre-notes.pdf) — it has traffic distribution and a sample request histogram.

We’re open to Redwood recommending a rate-limit package. Ideally, we want a predictable billing model and an ability to burst to 3k for short durations without significant throttling.

Happy to do the prep session — Diane and I are available Tue/Wed next week in the 9–11am PT window.

—Ethan
Ethan Grant
CTO, Acme Analytics
ethan.grant@acmeanalytics.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Grant <ethan.grant@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-04T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & concurrency (recap + next steps)

Ethan — this is great, thanks for the details and the SRE notes. Next steps from Redwood’s side: 

1) Marcus (cc’d) will draft a load-test / concurrency-qualification plan that mirrors your histogram and connection model (HTTP/2 multiplexing + ~500 persistent connections). Expect that doc by EOD tomorrow.

2) Rate limits & quota options: here are the pragmatic options we discussed verbally — we’ll formalize in an offer:
   - Option A (Hosted, default): standard account limits with adaptive throttling (good for non-critical launches). Default per-account concurrency throttle kicks in around 600 concurrent requests; burst token bucket allows short spikes but may cause retries.
   - Option B (Reserved concurrency): a dedicated concurrency quota (e.g., reserved 3k concurrency) on shared infra — predictable throughput and billing. Suitable if you want predictable latency during peaks.
   - Option C (Dedicated capacity): entire Dedicated pool (SLA-backed), for the lowest-latency/p95 guarantees and large sustained throughput.

Given your numbers (sustained ~1k, peaks 2.5k, burst to 3k), my recommendation is Option B as the right balance. We can size a reserved quota of 3k with an agreed-on burst buffer for launches.

3) For streaming start-time requirements (<100ms), Marcus will validate that we can achieve the prefix streaming behavior on your request size/seq length in our qualification run. If we see consistent misalignment, we can propose a lightweight Dedicated node group to guarantee the P95 targets.

Attachments: redwood-slo-table.pdf, load-test-plan.md

Can you confirm the preferred window for the load-test prep session (Tue/Wed 9–11am PT) and whether Diane should be the point of contact for scheduling? Once Marcus posts the plan, we’ll lock a test time.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Grant <ethan.grant@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Diane Lopez <diane.lopez@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & concurrency (recap + next steps)

Perfect — thanks Marissa. Tue (2026-08-10) at 10am PT works for us for the prep session. Diane will be the POC for scheduling and SRE questions.

We’re aligned on Option B for reserved concurrency; please include indicative pricing for the 3k reserved quota in the follow-up. Looking forward to Marcus’s plan.

Best,
Ethan
